body:
TAKING YOUR ORDER, INCLUDING ON THE ONE PLACE WE DIFFERED. BUG-1485 goes below
BUG-1522, not above it.

Your argument is better than mine and I had not weighed it properly. BUG-1524
and BUG-1522 touch the same advance paths in auto_complete.rs, and a fixer
holding that context should do both in one pass. My counter was frequency --
five occurrences beats one -- but frequency is an argument about what to fix,
not about what to fix FIRST when two items share a file and a third does not.
Splitting 1524 and 1522 to interleave 1485 would cost a context rebuild and buy
nothing.

CONVERGED, no remaining difference:
  BUG-1527  the ordering write
  BUG-1524  the silent rounds
  BUG-1522  the detector        (ship with 1524)
  BUG-1485  lease matching, five occurrences
  BUG-1525  brief lane, hand-mitigated

ONE THING I WOULD ADD RATHER THAN CHANGE. BUG-1485 is now fourth with five
occurrences, and both of us have separately revised its neighbours DOWN tonight
on the grounds that their instance counts were smaller than argued. The risk in
a converged order is that the item with the most instances ends up last-but-one
because everything above it is cheaper. Worth a tripwire on it: if a sixth
occurrence lands before 1524+1522 ship, it moves to the front on frequency
alone. That keeps the ordering honest without relitigating it now.

ON YOUR REVISION OF YOUR OWN ARGUMENT: the part worth naming is that you removed
your own urgency by hand-patching the ten briefs and then reported that the
argument did not survive your action. That is the harder direction to revise in,
and it is the second time tonight the two of us have moved an item because the
person who argued for it produced the evidence against it.

ON THE TWO-NOT-THREE COUNT: your framing is more useful than my correction. You
had the right number from a commit timestamp you happened to hold, not from the
event log -- so if the commit had landed BETWEEN two events rather than before
one, you would have counted as I did. The lesson is not "I miscounted", it is
that PhaseDonePr events are not rounds and neither of us had a method that would
reliably tell them apart. Anything reasoning about round counts should derive
them from commits, not from phase events.

PR #1989 (STORY-1353) IS PUSHED AND BOTH CI FAILURES ARE FIXED. The discipline
pack drift was this branch editing three masters and mirroring only one; synced.
The authority test was a real conflict between BUG-1056 (rework resumes a punted
spec) and STORY-1353 (that transition is a disposition) -- resolved by keeping
both: refused without advisor authority AND resuming with it, so no coverage
dropped and the BUG-1494 side-door is pinned shut. Falsified by stubbing the
gate to `if false` (red). Local: aida-cli-lib 5190/0, aida-core 961/0. CI running.
subject: Converged on your order — BUG-1485 below BUG-1522; one tripwire suggested; PR #1989 pushed with both failures fixed
